Cosmetic Dentistry

# Smile Makeover: What It Is and Who It's For

Discover how a comprehensive smile makeover can transform your appearance, boost your confidence, and give you the radiant smile you've always wanted. Learn about treatments, timelines, and what to expect.

January 20, 2026
8 min read
by Dr. Vidya Sahithi Atluri, MDS

## What Exactly Is a Smile Makeover?

A smile makeover isn't just about whitening your teeth or fixing one small problem. It's a comprehensive cosmetic plan designed specifically for you. It combines multiple dental treatments to address all the things about your smile that bother you, creating a harmonious, naturally beautiful result that complements your face and personality.

Rather than treating dental issues in isolation, a smile makeover takes a holistic approach. Your dentist evaluates your entire smile—the color, shape, alignment, gum line, and overall appearance—then develops a personalized plan to transform it. Some patients need just two or three treatments; others benefit from a more extensive combination.

The goal isn't to create a fake-looking celebrity smile. It's to enhance your natural beauty, boost your confidence, and help you feel like the best version of yourself.

## Who Benefits From a Smile Makeover?

If any of these describe you, you might be an excellent candidate for a smile makeover:

### Stained or Discolored Teeth

Years of coffee, tea, red wine, or smoking can leave your teeth looking dull and yellowed. Professional whitening can restore brightness, and for stubborn stains, veneers or bonding offer longer-lasting solutions.

### Gaps Between Teeth

Diastema—the technical term for gaps between teeth—can be closed with bonding, veneers, or orthodontics. The best option depends on the size of the gap and whether your bite needs correction.

### Crooked or Misaligned Teeth

Misaligned teeth affect both appearance and function. Orthodontics (traditional braces or clear aligners) can straighten your teeth, while veneers can create the appearance of straighter teeth without moving them.

### Chipped or Cracked Teeth

Accidents happen. Bonding can repair small chips, while more significant damage might require a crown or veneer for a more permanent, natural-looking fix.

### Uneven Gum Line

If your gums are too visible when you smile (often called a "gummy smile"), or if your gum line is uneven, gum contouring can reshape your gums for a more balanced appearance.

### Worn Down Teeth

Teeth grinding, acid reflux, or decades of use can wear teeth down, making them look shorter and affecting your bite. Crowns or bonding can restore their shape and size.

### Missing Teeth

Gaps from missing teeth not only affect appearance but also impact your bite and can lead to bone loss. Implants, bridges, or dentures can fill these gaps and restore your smile's completeness.

The bottom line? If there's anything about your smile that makes you feel self-conscious or unhappy, a smile makeover might be right for you.

## Common Treatments Included in a Smile Makeover

Depending on your goals and concerns, your smile makeover might include any combination of these treatments:

### Professional Teeth Whitening

The most popular cosmetic treatment, professional whitening uses custom trays and professional-strength bleaching gel to brighten your teeth by several shades. Results typically last 6 months to 2 years, depending on your habits and maintenance.

### Porcelain Veneers

Veneers are thin, custom-made shells bonded to the front of your teeth. They can correct stains, gaps, minor misalignment, and shape issues. Veneers look incredibly natural and are incredibly durable, lasting 10-15 years with proper care.

### Dental Crowns

Crowns completely cover damaged teeth, providing both structural support and cosmetic improvement. They're often used for teeth that are cracked, severely decayed, or significantly worn down.

### Composite Bonding

This quick, affordable option uses tooth-colored composite resin to repair chips, close small gaps, change tooth shape, or cover stains. While not as durable as veneers or crowns, bonding is a great starting point for many patients.

### Orthodontic Treatment

Traditional braces, clear aligners like Invisalign, or other orthodontic systems can straighten your teeth over 18-24 months. Many adults are surprised by how discreet modern orthodontics can be.

### Gum Contouring

Using lasers or traditional sculpting, your dentist can reshape your gums to create a more balanced appearance. This is especially helpful for people with a "gummy smile" or uneven gum lines.

### Dental Implants

For missing teeth, implants are the gold standard. They look, feel, and function like natural teeth and can last a lifetime with proper care. Implants also prevent bone loss that occurs with missing teeth.

At Krishna Dental, we'll evaluate which combination of treatments will give you the best results for your unique smile.

## The Consultation: Starting Your Smile Makeover Journey

Your smile makeover begins with a comprehensive consultation. Here's what to expect:

### Smile Analysis

Your dentist will examine your teeth, gums, and overall facial structure. They'll look at tooth color, shape, size, alignment, and spacing. They'll also assess your gum health and how your smile relates to your face and personality. This isn't about judgment—it's about understanding your unique features and goals.

### Digital Smile Design

Using advanced imaging technology, we can show you a preview of what your smile could look like after treatment. We might adjust the shape, shade, or proportions of your teeth based on your feedback. You get to see the plan before any treatment begins, ensuring you're excited about the direction.

### Discussion of Concerns and Goals

Share everything that bothers you about your current smile. Maybe it's the color, the shape, the alignment, or something less obvious. We'll listen carefully and help you prioritize which concerns to address first. Some issues are cosmetic; some also affect function. We'll discuss both.

### Personalized Treatment Plan

Based on the analysis and your goals, we'll create a step-by-step treatment plan. We'll explain what each treatment involves, how long it takes, what results to expect, and the cost. We'll also discuss alternatives, so you can make informed choices about which treatments are right for you.

### Timeline and Sequence

We'll map out when each treatment should happen and in what order. Some treatments might need to be done before others. For example, if you're getting implants, they need time to integrate into your bone before we place a crown. Other treatments, like whitening and bonding, can happen simultaneously.

Pro Tip: Bring photos of smiles you admire, or describe what you love about your current smile. This helps us understand your aesthetic preferences and ensure we're creating a smile that feels authentically you.

## Before and After: What Results to Expect

The transformation that a smile makeover can achieve is remarkable—but it's important to have realistic expectations about what's possible.

### Realistic Transformations

A smile makeover can correct discoloration, close gaps, repair chips, straighten teeth, reshape your gums, and replace missing teeth. Combined, these changes can be truly life-changing. Your new smile will look natural—not overly bright or artificially perfect, but genuinely better than before.

### What Modern Dentistry Can Achieve

Thanks to advances in materials and techniques, cosmetic dentistry results look more natural than ever. Porcelain veneers and crowns can match your surrounding teeth perfectly. Composite bonding blends seamlessly with your natural tooth structure. Even teeth straightened with clear aligners look completely natural once treatment is complete.

### The Confidence Factor

While we can't promise to solve all your life's problems, our patients consistently report that having a smile they're proud of transforms their confidence. They smile more freely, take better photos, feel more comfortable in social situations, and even perform better in professional settings. The psychological boost is real and significant.

### Long-Term Results

The longevity of your results depends on the treatments chosen and your maintenance habits. Whitening effects typically fade over time and need periodic touch-ups. Veneers last 10-15 years. Crowns can last 15-20 years or longer. Bonding lasts 5-7 years. Implants can last a lifetime. Orthodontic results are permanent as long as you wear your retainer. We'll give you specific care instructions to maximize the lifespan of each treatment.

## How Long Does a Smile Makeover Take?

There's no single answer—it depends on which treatments you're having and their complexity.

### Quick Makeovers (3-6 Months)

If you're doing teeth whitening, bonding, and maybe one or two veneers, you could see results in as little as 3-6 months. These treatments are faster and don't require the teeth to be prepared extensively.

### Moderate Makeovers (6-12 Months)

Adding more veneers, multiple crowns, or combining treatments with some orthodontics typically takes 6-12 months. There may be waiting periods between stages as we assess results and prepare for the next step.

### Comprehensive Makeovers (12-24 Months)

If orthodontic treatment is involved—whether to straighten teeth before veneer placement or as a standalone treatment—expect 18-24 months. Dental implants also require time as the implant integrates with your bone (usually 3-6 months) before we place the crown. Some patients also choose to space treatments out for budget reasons, extending the timeline.

### Maintenance Timeline

Once your makeover is complete, you'll need regular maintenance. Whitening touch-ups might happen annually or every 18 months. Veneers and crowns need the same care as natural teeth—regular brushing, flossing, and dental check-ups.

The good news? You don't have to wait for everything at once. Many patients do some treatments immediately and plan others down the road. This approach spreads costs and allows you to adjust as you see results.

## Is It Painful? Recovery and Comfort

This is a common concern, and we want to reassure you: most cosmetic treatments have minimal discomfort.

### Whitening

Professional whitening is painless, though some people experience temporary sensitivity to cold. This usually subsides within a few days after treatment.

### Veneers and Crowns

To prepare teeth for veneers or crowns, we remove a thin layer of enamel. This is done under local anesthesia, so you won't feel pain—just vibration and water spray. After anesthesia wears off, you might have mild sensitivity for a day or two, but this is manageable with over-the-counter pain relief if needed. Most patients report no pain, just slight soreness.

### Bonding

Composite bonding is completely painless. No shots or anesthesia needed. Some patients feel a slight cold sensation from the restoration materials, but it's quick and easy.

### Gum Contouring

Gum reshaping is done under local anesthesia and is generally painless. You might feel pressure or vibration from the laser or scalpel, but not pain. Some mild soreness for a day or two is normal.

### Orthodontics

You won't feel pain, but you might feel pressure and soreness for a few days after your aligners are tightened or your braces are adjusted. This is manageable and decreases over time as your teeth shift.

### Implants

Implant placement is done under local anesthesia (or sedation if you prefer). You won't feel pain, just pressure. Some soreness and swelling for a few days after is normal and easily managed with ice packs and pain medication if needed.

Our Commitment: We use modern anesthetic techniques, the latest equipment, and gentle handling to minimize any discomfort. If you're nervous about dental treatment, let us know—we have options to help you feel comfortable.

## Maintaining Your New Smile

Your smile makeover represents an investment in yourself. Here's how to keep it looking beautiful for years:

### Daily Care

- Brush twice daily with a soft-bristled toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste
- Floss daily to clean between teeth and under the gum line
- Use mouthwash to remove bacteria and freshen your breath
- Avoid chewing on hard objects (ice, pens, your nails) which can crack teeth or chip restorations

### Dietary Choices

Some foods and drinks are particularly harsh on teeth and restorations. Limit acidic foods and beverages, which can erode enamel and weaken bonds. Minimize dark-colored drinks like coffee, tea, and red wine, which can stain teeth and restorations. If you consume staining substances, use a straw and rinse with water afterward.

### Avoid Smoking and Tobacco

Tobacco stains teeth and restorations and increases your risk of gum disease and oral cancer. If you smoke, quitting is one of the best things you can do for your smile—and your health.

### Protect Against Grinding

If you grind your teeth at night, wear a mouthguard to protect your natural teeth and restorations. Grinding can crack teeth, loosen crowns, and shorten the life of veneers.

### Regular Dental Visits

Visit your dentist every 6 months for professional cleaning and check-ups. These visits allow us to monitor your restorations, catch any issues early, and keep your entire mouth healthy.

### Whitening Touch-Ups

If you've had professional whitening, you'll likely want touch-up treatments annually or every 18 months to maintain the brightness. We can provide take-home trays or do in-office treatments as needed.

## Cost Considerations and Planning

Smile makeovers are an investment, and it's important to understand the financial aspect before you start.

### Price Varies Widely

There's no fixed price for a smile makeover because every smile is different. A simple makeover involving one or two treatments might cost a few thousand rupees. A comprehensive makeover with multiple treatments could cost significantly more. During your consultation, we'll provide a detailed cost estimate for each treatment and the total plan.

### Payment Plans and Financing

We understand that comprehensive dental treatment is a significant investment. At Krishna Dental, we offer flexible payment plans to make treatment more affordable. We also work with various financing options so you can get the smile of your dreams without breaking the bank.

### Phased Approach

You don't need to do everything at once. Many patients choose to do treatments in phases, starting with what bothers them most, then planning other treatments down the road. This spreads costs over time and allows you to adjust based on results.

### Insurance and Coverage

Cosmetic treatments typically aren't covered by insurance because they're elective. However, if a treatment serves a functional purpose (like a crown that also improves appearance, or braces for bite correction), a portion might be covered. We can help you understand what your insurance will and won't cover.

### Long-Term Value

When considering cost, think about value and longevity. A quality restoration that lasts 15 years is a better investment than a cheaper option that needs replacement in 5 years. We use the best materials and techniques to ensure your results last.

Teeth Whitening: Professional vs At-Home — Complete Guide | Krishna Multispeciality Dental Hospital Gudivada

Cosmetic Dentistry

# Teeth Whitening: Professional vs At-Home

What actually works, what doesn't, and how to get the safest, longest-lasting results for your smile.

📅 March 24, 2026
⏱️ 8 min read
✍️ Dr. Vidya Sahithi Atluri, MDS

## Why Do Teeth Become Discoloured?

Before choosing a whitening method, it helps to understand why teeth lose their brightness. Discolouration falls into two main categories: extrinsic staining (stains on the outer surface of the enamel) and intrinsic discolouration (staining within the tooth structure itself). These respond very differently to whitening treatment.

Extrinsic stains — the most common type — come from pigmented compounds in food and drink. Coffee, tea, red wine, turmeric, and tobacco are the biggest culprits. These stains accumulate on the pellicle (a thin film on the enamel surface) and respond well to both professional whitening and scaling/polishing. This is the kind of staining that most people are trying to address.

Intrinsic discolouration occurs within the dentin layer beneath the enamel. It can result from tetracycline antibiotic use during childhood (which causes greyish-brown banding), excessive fluoride during tooth development (fluorosis — white spots or brown patches), trauma to a tooth, or the natural yellowing of dentin with age. Intrinsic staining is much harder to treat and may not respond to standard whitening at all. Severe cases may require veneers or bonding instead.

First step: a professional clean

Before any whitening treatment, a professional scaling and polishing removes surface plaque and tartar. This alone can brighten your smile noticeably — and it's essential for even whitening results, since whitening gel cannot penetrate plaque or calculus deposits.

## Professional In-Clinic Whitening

Professional whitening uses high-concentration hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide gels (typically 25–40% concentration) applied directly to your teeth under controlled conditions. The dentist first places a protective barrier over your gums, then applies the whitening gel to tooth surfaces. A curing light or laser may be used to activate the gel and accelerate the whitening process.

The entire procedure takes approximately 60–90 minutes. Most patients see 6–10 shades of improvement in a single session. The primary advantages of in-clinic whitening are speed, intensity, and safety — your gums are fully protected, concentrations are precisely controlled, and any sensitivity is managed in real time.

Some patients experience temporary tooth sensitivity during or after the procedure. This typically resolves within 24–48 hours. Using a sensitivity toothpaste for a week before treatment reduces this significantly. Patients with existing dental work (crowns, veneers, fillings) should discuss realistic expectations with their dentist — whitening only works on natural enamel.

## Dentist-Prescribed At-Home Whitening Trays

Custom-fitted whitening trays made from impressions of your teeth hold a lower-concentration whitening gel (10–22% carbamide peroxide) against your teeth for several hours per day, typically worn at night while you sleep. Results emerge over 2–3 weeks.

The key advantage over over-the-counter alternatives is the custom fit. A well-fitted tray ensures the gel contacts all tooth surfaces evenly and stays away from gum tissue. Ill-fitting generic trays allow gel to leak onto gums (causing irritation) and miss tooth surfaces (causing uneven whitening).

Custom at-home trays are excellent for gradual whitening with minimal sensitivity. Many dentists combine in-clinic whitening with at-home trays — a professional session for immediate impact, followed by at-home maintenance to refine and maintain results.

## Over-the-Counter Products: What Actually Works?

Whitening toothpastes work primarily through mild abrasives that polish off surface stains. They cannot chemically bleach teeth. Some contain low concentrations of hydrogen peroxide or blue covarine (a pigment that creates an optical whitening effect). Results are subtle and slow, but they're useful for maintenance between professional treatments.

Whitening strips contain peroxide-impregnated plastic strips applied to front teeth. Results are real but limited — typically 2–4 shades over 2 weeks. They only cover the front teeth and don't conform to tooth curves well, often leaving unwhitened patches. Overuse causes sensitivity.

LED whitening kits sold online have flooded the market. Most use low concentrations of peroxide that are the same or lower than whitening toothpastes in effective bleaching power. The light itself has no significant whitening effect at home intensities. Many simply don't work as advertised.

Charcoal products are abrasive and can scratch enamel with repeated use. There is no clinical evidence that activated charcoal whitens teeth — and it may make them more susceptible to staining by removing the smooth, protective enamel surface.

## Who Is a Good Candidate for Teeth Whitening?

Teeth whitening works best on patients with mild to moderate extrinsic or age-related yellowing. Healthy teeth and gums are a prerequisite — cavities and gum disease must be treated before whitening. Pregnant women should avoid whitening until after delivery.

Patients with heavily stained or intrinsically discoloured teeth (tetracycline staining, fluorosis) may achieve limited results from whitening alone. Veneers or composite bonding may be more appropriate for dramatic colour change in these cases.

Patients with multiple visible restorations (crowns, composite fillings on front teeth) should have a thorough consultation before whitening to understand which teeth will and won't respond, and whether replacements would be needed to match the new shade.

## Maintaining Your Results

The "white diet" for the first 48 hours after whitening is important — avoid coffee, tea, red wine, curries, beetroot, and berries. Your enamel pores are slightly more open immediately after whitening and stain more readily. After 48 hours, normal foods are fine.

Using a straw for coffee and tea reduces direct contact with teeth. Rinsing with water after consuming staining foods helps. A whitening toothpaste used 2–3 times per week maintains results. A touch-up with at-home trays every 6–12 months keeps your smile bright long-term.

Written by Dr. Vidya Sahithi Atluri, MDS

Dr. Vidya offers professional teeth whitening at Krishna Multispeciality Dental Hospital, Gudivada — using clinical-grade whitening systems that deliver safe, consistent, lasting results.

## Frequently asked questions

How many shades can teeth whitening achieve?

Professional in-clinic whitening typically achieves 6–10 shades of improvement in a single session. At-home trays achieve 4–6 shades over 2–3 weeks. Results vary depending on the type and cause of staining. Consult the team at Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada for details.

Does teeth whitening damage enamel?

Professional teeth whitening, when done correctly with dentist-prescribed concentrations at Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada, does not permanently damage enamel. Temporary sensitivity is common but resolves within 24–48 hours. Over-the-counter products used excessively can cause enamel erosion.

How long does teeth whitening last?

Professional whitening results typically last 1–3 years with good maintenance. Avoiding staining foods and drinks, using a whitening toothpaste, and doing occasional at-home touch-up treatments from our Gudivada clinic extends results significantly.

Can I whiten my teeth if I have crowns or veneers?

Whitening agents only work on natural tooth enamel — they cannot change the colour of crowns, veneers, or fillings. If you whiten natural teeth, your restorations may no longer match. Discuss this with Dr. Vidya Sahithi in Gudivada before starting whitening.

How much does teeth whitening cost in Gudivada?

Professional teeth whitening at Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada is significantly more affordable than in major cities, while using the same clinical-grade materials. Visit our contact page or clinic for current pricing and a free smile assessment.

Oral Surgery

# Wisdom Tooth Pain? Here's What You Should Know

Jan 8, 2026
7 min read
By Krishna Dental Team

Everything you need to know about wisdom tooth pain: why it happens, what to do about it, and when extraction might be necessary. Expert insights for Gudivada residents.

## Why Do Wisdom Teeth Cause Problems?

Wisdom teeth — your third molars — are the last teeth to erupt, typically appearing in your late teens or twenties. For many people, they cause no problems at all. But for millions of others, they're a source of pain, infection, and complications that often requires extraction.

The reason is evolutionary: our ancestors had larger jaws that accommodated thirty-two teeth comfortably. Modern humans, however, have smaller jaws — most of us simply don't have enough space for all four wisdom teeth to erupt properly.

When there's not enough room, wisdom teeth can become "impacted," meaning they get stuck or grow at an angle. This can lead to crowding, infection, cysts, damage to neighbouring teeth, and significant pain. If you're in Gudivada and experiencing persistent jaw pain, especially in the back of your mouth, wisdom teeth might be the culprit.

## Recognizing Wisdom Tooth Symptoms

Not all wisdom tooth problems announce themselves loudly. Some develop gradually, while others come on suddenly. Here are the key symptoms to watch for:

### Pain and Discomfort

The most obvious sign is pain in the back of your mouth, jaw, or even extending to your ear. This pain can range from mild and intermittent to severe and constant. You might notice it's worse when eating or chewing.

### Swelling and Redness

When a wisdom tooth is partially erupted or infected, the gum around it often becomes swollen, red, and tender. This is caused by inflammation and bacterial colonization of the area.

### Difficulty Opening Your Mouth

Some people with impacted wisdom teeth experience trismus — difficulty opening the mouth fully or limited jaw movement. This can make eating and speaking uncomfortable.

### Infection Signs

If a wisdom tooth becomes infected, you might notice bad breath, pus or discharge from the site, or even a fever. These are signs that the infection is active and needs immediate attention from a dentist in Gudivada or Krishna district.

### Damage to Nearby Teeth

Wisdom teeth that grow at an angle can press against and damage the second molar next to them. You might experience pain in that tooth or notice it's becoming loose.

### Cavity Formation

Impacted or partially erupted wisdom teeth are harder to clean properly, making them susceptible to decay. You might develop cavities that cause sensitivity or pain.

### Jaw Stiffness

Swelling deep in the jaw can cause stiffness and reduced mobility, making it difficult to enjoy normal activities.

## Types of Wisdom Tooth Impaction

Impaction is classified based on how the tooth is positioned relative to the jawbone and neighbouring teeth. Understanding the type can help you grasp why extraction might be recommended:

### Mesial Impaction

The tooth is angled forward, toward the front of the mouth. This is the most common type and is often the most likely to cause problems with the neighbouring molar.

### Distal Impaction

The tooth is angled backward, away from the front. This is the least common type and usually causes fewer problems than other types.

### Vertical Impaction

The tooth is growing straight down but is trapped beneath the gum and bone. It's completely stuck and has no room to erupt naturally.

### Horizontal Impaction

The tooth is lying on its side, completely horizontal within the jawbone. This is the most severe form and typically requires surgical extraction.

At Krishna Dental in Gudivada, we use digital imaging to determine the exact position of your impacted teeth and recommend the most appropriate treatment.

When to Seek Help: If you're experiencing pain around your wisdom teeth that lasts more than a few days, or if you notice signs of infection (swelling, pus, fever), don't wait. Contact Krishna Dental immediately for an evaluation.

## Home Remedies for Temporary Relief

While home remedies won't cure an impacted or infected wisdom tooth, they can provide temporary relief while you arrange to see your dentist. Here are evidence-based strategies:

### Saltwater Rinses

Mix half a teaspoon of salt in warm water and rinse your mouth gently, especially around the affected area. This reduces inflammation and kills bacteria. Do this 3–4 times daily, especially after meals.

### Cold Compress

Apply a cold pack wrapped in a towel to the outside of your cheek for 15–20 minutes at a time, with 15-minute breaks. Cold reduces swelling and numbs the area temporarily. This is particularly effective in the first 24–48 hours after symptoms start.

### Over-the-Counter Pain Relief

Ibuprofen, paracetamol, or aspirin can help manage pain and reduce inflammation. Follow the dosage on the package, and don't exceed the recommended daily limit.

### Soft Foods

Stick to soft, cool foods like yoghurt, ice cream, mashed potatoes, smoothies, and soup. Avoid chewing on the side where your wisdom teeth are located.

### Avoid Irritants

Don't use a straw, as the suction can dislodge clots and worsen pain. Avoid smoking and alcohol, which can slow healing and increase irritation.

### Gentle Oral Hygiene

Continue brushing and flossing, but be gentle around the affected area. Keeping your mouth clean reduces the risk of infection.

### Clove Oil

A small amount of clove oil on the affected area can provide temporary numbing relief due to its natural eugenol content. However, this is strictly temporary and won't address the underlying problem.

Important: These remedies provide temporary comfort only. They won't solve the underlying issue. If your pain persists for more than a week or worsens, you need professional dental care from Krishna Dental in Gudivada.

## When to See a Dentist

You should schedule an appointment with your dentist in the following situations:

- Pain in the back of your mouth lasting more than a few days.
- Visible swelling in your face or jaw.
- Difficulty swallowing or breathing (seek emergency care immediately for this).
- Signs of infection: fever, pus, severe swelling, or bad taste in your mouth.
- Damage to neighbouring teeth.
- Recurrent problems with wisdom teeth.
- Pain that doesn't improve with over-the-counter pain relief.

Early intervention by a dentist in Krishna district can prevent complications and often save you from needing extraction down the road. At Krishna Dental, we assess each case individually to determine the best course of action — extraction isn't always necessary, but sometimes it's the best option for your long-term health.

## The Wisdom Tooth Extraction Process

If your dentist recommends extraction, here's what to expect:

### Before the Procedure

You'll have a consultation where X-rays are taken and your medical history is reviewed. Your dentist will discuss anaesthesia options and any pre-operative instructions. If possible, avoid eating for 6–8 hours before your procedure.

### Anaesthesia

You'll receive local anaesthesia to numb the area. Some patients opt for sedation, which keeps you relaxed and comfortable throughout the procedure. General anaesthesia is reserved for complex cases.

### Extraction

The dentist will remove any gum and bone covering the tooth, gently elevate it, and carefully extract it. For impacted teeth, the tooth might be removed in pieces to minimize trauma. The procedure typically takes 20 to 45 minutes, depending on complexity.

### After Extraction

Gauze is placed in the socket to stop bleeding. You might notice some oozing for a few hours, which is normal. A blood clot forms, which is crucial for healing.

## Recovery Timeline: What to Expect

Recovery from wisdom tooth extraction varies based on the complexity of the extraction and how well you follow aftercare instructions.

### First 24 Hours

- Bleeding may continue for a few hours. Bite down on gauze for 30–45 minutes if needed.
- Swelling and bruising typically peak during this period.
- Pain is usually mild to moderate and manageable with prescribed or over-the-counter pain relief.
- Rest is important — avoid strenuous activity.

### Days 2–7

- Swelling usually peaks around day 2–3 and gradually improves.
- Pain decreases as the socket heals.
- You can slowly return to normal activities.
- Continue ice therapy for the first 48 hours, then switch to heat if swelling persists.

### Weeks 2–4

- Most swelling and bruising resolve.
- You can resume normal eating and exercise.
- The socket begins filling in with bone and soft tissue.

### Months 3–6

- Complete bone fill-in occurs beneath the surface.
- If dental implants or bridges were planned, this is typically when they're placed.

Complete healing takes several months, but most patients return to normal within a week or two.

## Foods to Eat After Wisdom Tooth Extraction

What you eat after extraction matters. Soft, nutrient-dense foods support healing without disturbing the socket:

- Soups and broths: Nourishing and easy to consume.
- Yoghurt: Protein-rich and soothing.
- Mashed potatoes: Soft and filling.
- Smoothies: Nutrient-dense but avoid using a straw.
- Applesauce: Soft and naturally sweet.
- Cottage cheese: High in protein.
- Scrambled eggs: Soft, protein-rich.
- Ice cream: Cool and soothing (sugar-free is better).

Avoid hot foods, crunchy foods, sticky foods, and anything that requires vigorous chewing for at least a week.

## Potential Complications to Watch For

While extraction is usually straightforward, be aware of these potential complications:

### Dry Socket

This occurs when the blood clot in the socket is dislodged, exposing the bone beneath. It causes significant pain and requires professional treatment. Avoid smoking and using straws to prevent this.

### Infection

Signs include increased swelling, pus, fever, or worsening pain after the first few days. Contact your dentist immediately if you suspect infection.

### Nerve Damage

Rarely, the inferior alveolar nerve (which supplies sensation to your lower lip and chin) or lingual nerve (which supplies the tongue) is temporarily or permanently affected. This causes numbness or tingling. Usually, it's temporary.

### Excessive Bleeding

Some patients bleed more than expected. If bleeding doesn't stop after 3–4 hours of gentle biting on gauze, contact your dentist.

Most patients experience no complications. At Krishna Dental, we provide detailed aftercare instructions to minimize risks and ensure smooth healing.

## Do All Wisdom Teeth Need Removal?

Not necessarily. Many people have wisdom teeth that erupt normally without problems. Extraction is recommended when:

- The tooth is impacted or partially erupted.
- There's infection or severe decay.
- The tooth is damaging neighbouring teeth.
- There's a cyst or other pathology around the tooth.
- The tooth is causing persistent pain or swelling.
- There's simply no room in your jaw for the tooth to erupt properly.

If your wisdom teeth are healthy, properly positioned, and don't cause problems, there's no reason to remove them. At Krishna Dental, we assess each tooth individually and recommend extraction only when it's truly beneficial for your oral health.

- Root Canal Treatment
- Dental Implants

## Frequently asked questions

At what age do wisdom teeth come in?

Wisdom teeth (third molars) typically emerge between ages 17 and 25. Some people never develop them; others may have up to four. Visit Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada if they cause discomfort during eruption.

How do I know if my wisdom tooth is impacted?

Signs of an impacted wisdom tooth include pain or pressure at the back of the jaw, swollen or red gums behind the last molar, difficulty opening the mouth fully, and bad taste in the area. Dr. Vidya Sahithi in Gudivada can diagnose this via X-ray.

Can I manage wisdom tooth pain at home?

Temporary relief includes ibuprofen, rinsing with warm salt water, and applying clove oil. These are not treatments — see a dentist in Gudivada as soon as possible as pain usually worsens without professional care at Krishna Dental Hospital.

Is wisdom tooth removal always necessary?

Not always. If a wisdom tooth is fully erupted, properly positioned, and easy to clean, it may not need removal. However, impacted, partially erupted, or decay-prone wisdom teeth are usually better removed at Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada.

How long is recovery after wisdom tooth removal?

Most people recover fully within 3–7 days. A blood clot forms in the socket (do not disturb it). Soft foods, no smoking, and gentle rinsing are key to smooth recovery. Follow post-op instructions from our Gudivada clinic.

Restorative Dentistry

# Crowns & Bridges

Restore damaged or missing teeth with custom-made crowns and bridges. Achieve a natural-looking smile that feels as good as it looks.

Book Appointment

Understanding treatment

## What are crowns and bridges?

A crown is a custom-made cap that covers a damaged or decayed tooth, restoring its shape, size, strength, and appearance. A bridge replaces one or more missing teeth by anchoring to adjacent natural teeth or implants.

Both solutions are permanent or semi-permanent, natural-looking, and restore full functionality to your teeth and smile. At Krishna Dental, we use advanced technology and premium materials to craft restorations that blend seamlessly with your natural teeth.

Material options

## Types of crowns we offer

### Zirconia crowns

Strongest and most durable option. Zirconia offers excellent biocompatibility, natural appearance, and resistance to staining. Perfect for visible teeth and high-stress areas.

### Porcelain crowns

Unmatched aesthetics and translucency that mimics natural teeth. Ideal for front teeth where appearance is paramount. Requires gentle care to avoid chipping.

### PFM (Porcelain-fused-to-metal)

Combines strength of metal with the beauty of porcelain. Offers excellent durability and aesthetics. A popular choice for back teeth where strength matters.

### Metal crowns

Gold or alloy crowns. The strongest and longest-lasting option with minimal wear. Most durable choice but less aesthetic — ideal for back molars.

Step by step

## How we create your crown or bridge

01

### Assessment & preparation

We examine the tooth and take X-rays to assess decay or damage. The tooth is gently prepared by removing decayed portions and shaping it to accommodate the crown.

02

### Impressions

Precise digital or traditional impressions are taken to ensure your crown fits perfectly. We also match the shade to blend with your natural teeth.

03

### Temporary crown

A temporary crown protects your prepared tooth while we craft your permanent restoration. This keeps your tooth functional and maintains appearance.

04

### Lab fabrication

Our experienced lab technicians craft your custom crown using premium materials. Every detail is perfected to match your natural tooth shape and shade.

05

### Final fitting

Your permanent crown is carefully fitted and adjusted for comfort and bite alignment. Once perfect, it's permanently cemented to provide lasting protection.

Why choose us

## Crown and bridge care you can trust

### Premium materials

We source the finest zirconia, porcelain, and metals from trusted labs. Your crown is built to last with materials that resist staining and wear.

### Precise fit

Using digital imaging and detailed impressions, we ensure your crown fits perfectly. Proper fit means comfort, longevity, and protection for your natural tooth.

### Natural aesthetics

Our crowns blend seamlessly with your natural teeth in shape, colour, and texture. No one will know you have a crown — it simply looks like your real tooth.

### Same-week turnaround

In many cases, we can complete your crown in one visit with advanced same-day technology. No need to wait weeks or walk around with a temporary crown.

Common questions

## Frequently asked questions

How long do dental crowns last?

With proper care and regular dental check-ups, a well-made crown can last 10 to 15 years or even longer. At Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada, we use premium materials like Zirconia or CAD/CAM ceramics that ensure structural durability and longevity.

What's the difference between a crown and a veneer?

A crown covers the entire tooth to restore shape and strength, whereas a veneer only covers the front surface for cosmetic enhancements. At our Gudivada practice, crowns are recommended for decayed or root canal-treated teeth, while veneers are ideal for minor cosmetic improvements.

Does getting a crown hurt?

No, dental crown procedures at Krishna Multispeciality Dental Hospital are designed to be completely pain-free. We use advanced localized anesthesia to numb the area, and our specialists in Gudivada perform the preparation with gentle care to ensure your absolute comfort.

What is the cost of crowns and bridges in Gudivada?

The cost of dental crowns and bridges in Gudivada depends on the material selected (such as Zirconia, E-Max porcelain, PFM, or metal) and the number of teeth. We offer competitive, transparent pricing at Krishna Dental with flexible EMI payment options. You can request a customized estimate through our contact page.

How should I care for my crown?

Care for your crown just like a natural tooth: brush twice daily, floss daily around the gumline, and avoid biting down on exceptionally hard objects. Regular 6-month check-ups at Krishna Multispeciality Dental Hospital in Gudivada will help ensure your restoration remains secure.

When do I need to replace my crown?

You may need to replace your crown if you notice chipping, cracks, significant wear, or gum recession exposing the tooth border. If your crown feels loose or painful, visit our Gudivada dental hospital immediately for a diagnostic X-ray and evaluation.

Preventive Care
# Teeth Cleaning & Scaling

A clean, healthy smile starts with professional care. Our gentle cleaning removes what brushing can't reach — the foundation of lasting oral health.

Book Appointment

Foundation of oral health
## Why professional cleaning matters

While daily brushing and flossing are essential, they cannot remove tartar (hardened plaque) that builds up on your teeth and below the gumline. Professional cleaning removes these stubborn deposits that lead to gum disease, tooth decay, and other oral health problems.

Professional scaling reaches deep below the gumline where bacteria hide and cause damage. Regular cleanings prevent serious gum disease, freshen your breath, and keep your natural smile bright and healthy for life.
Comprehensive cleaning
## What we clean

### Tartar & calculus removal

Our ultrasonic scalers break up and remove hardened tartar buildup that regular brushing cannot reach, restoring teeth to their natural surface.

### Plaque elimination

We remove soft plaque buildup that harbours harmful bacteria, preventing cavities and gum disease before they start.

### Stain removal

Professional polishing removes surface stains from coffee, tea, wine, and smoking, leaving your smile visibly brighter and fresher.

### Below-the-gumline cleaning

Our dentists carefully scale below your gumline to remove bacteria and buildup that cause gum disease, protecting your gums and bone.
Step by step
## The cleaning process
01
### Oral examination

We start by examining your teeth and gums for signs of decay, gum disease, or other issues. This helps us customise your cleaning to your specific needs.
02
### Ultrasonic scaling

Our modern ultrasonic scaler vibrates at a frequency that breaks up tartar and calculus buildup on the tooth surface and below the gumline, gently and efficiently.
03
### Hand scaling

For stubborn deposits and detailed work, especially below the gumline, our dentist uses hand scalers with precision and care to ensure no buildup is left behind.
04
### Polishing

A gentle polishing paste removes any remaining surface stains and leaves your teeth feeling smooth and looking bright. Your smile will feel refreshed and clean.
05
### Fluoride treatment

We apply a protective fluoride treatment that strengthens enamel and helps prevent cavities and sensitivity. This extra protection lasts for months.
Why choose us
## Why Krishna Dental

### Gentle ultrasonic tools

Our state-of-the-art ultrasonic scalers are effective yet gentle on teeth and gums, making the cleaning process comfortable even for sensitive patients.

### Thorough yet comfortable

We take time to clean thoroughly without rushing. Our dentists are trained to work gently, pausing if you need a break, ensuring your comfort throughout.

### Quick appointments

Most cleanings take 30-60 minutes, and we respect your time. We use efficient techniques and advanced tools to complete the procedure quickly without compromising quality.

### Preventive focus

We emphasize prevention to keep your teeth and gums healthy long-term. Our dentists provide personalised guidance on home care to extend the benefits of your cleaning.

## Frequently asked questions

How often should I get professional dental cleaning in Gudivada?

Most patients benefit from professional teeth cleaning and scaling at our Gudivada clinic every 6 months. We customize the schedule based on your gum health; those prone to calculus or gum inflammation in the Krishna district may require cleanings every 3 to 4 months.

Does scaling damage teeth at Krishna Dental Hospital?

No, professional scaling does not damage healthy tooth enamel. Our MDS specialists in Gudivada use advanced ultrasonic scalers designed to gently remove tartar deposits without harming the underlying tooth structure, followed by professional polishing.

Is dental cleaning painful at your Gudivada clinic?

Dental cleaning and scaling at our Gudivada practice is generally painless. For sensitive teeth or active gum inflammation, we use modern ultrasonic instruments with adjustable settings and can apply specialized desensitizing gels to ensure your absolute comfort.

How long does a cleaning appointment take in Gudivada?

A standard scaling and polishing session at our Gudivada dental practice typically takes 30 to 60 minutes. This efficient duration allows us to thoroughly clean below the gumline and polish all tooth surfaces for a fresh, healthy, and hygienic smile.

What is the cost of dental cleaning in Gudivada?

The cost of professional teeth cleaning and scaling in Gudivada depends on the extent of tartar buildup and plaque deposits. Krishna Dental Hospital offers transparent pricing and comprehensive oral health evaluations. Please contact us online for a personalized quote.

What is the difference between scaling and regular brushing in Gudivada?

Regular brushing removes soft plaque daily, but professional scaling is required to remove hardened tartar (calculus) that binds to teeth. At our Gudivada clinic, professional scaling safely eliminates tartar below the gumline, which is critical to preventing gingivitis and periodontitis in the Krishna region.

General Dentistry

# Dental Fillings

Restore cavities and protect your teeth with tooth-coloured fillings. Strong, durable, and beautiful — all in one visit.

Book Appointment

Understanding fillings

## What are dental fillings?

A dental filling is a treatment to repair a tooth that has been damaged by decay. The infected or decayed portion is removed, the tooth is cleaned and disinfected, and the cavity is filled with a protective material.

Fillings restore the tooth's structure and function while preventing the decay from spreading deeper. Modern fillings are comfortable, aesthetic, and can last many years with proper care. At Krishna Dental, we use high-quality materials and painless techniques.

Material options

## Types of fillings

### Composite (tooth-coloured)

Aesthetic, tooth-matched fillings that bond directly to the tooth. Ideal for visible areas. Durable and look natural.

### Ceramic / Porcelain

Highly durable and stain-resistant. Matches tooth colour beautifully. Lasts longer than composite. Premium option.

### Glass ionomer

Releases fluoride to strengthen the tooth and prevent decay. Great for root cavities and primary teeth. Aesthetic option.

### Amalgam (silver)

Strong and highly durable. Best for back teeth under heavy chewing pressure. Contains safe amounts of mercury.

Step by step

## The filling procedure

01

### Examination & X-ray

We examine the cavity and take a digital X-ray to assess the size and depth of decay. This helps us choose the best filling material and approach.

02

### Anaesthesia

The tooth and surrounding gum are numbed with local anaesthesia. You'll be comfortable throughout — most patients feel only pressure, not pain.

03

### Decay removal

We carefully remove all decayed and infected tissue using precision instruments. The tooth is then cleaned, shaped, and prepared for the filling material.

04

### Filling placement

The filling material is carefully placed into the cavity and shaped to match the natural tooth contour. For composite fillings, we use a special light to harden the material.

05

### Bite adjustment

We check that your bite feels natural and comfortable. Any excess material is polished away, leaving a smooth, natural-looking filling.

Why choose us

## Why Krishna Dental

### Painless procedures

Modern anaesthesia and gentle techniques mean no pain during treatment. You'll be relaxed and comfortable throughout.

### Tooth-coloured materials

We use high-quality composite and ceramic fillings that match your natural tooth colour for an invisible restoration.

### Single-visit completion

Most fillings are completed in one appointment. Get your tooth restored and back to normal function immediately.

### Affordable care

Transparent pricing with no hidden costs. We offer flexible payment options so quality dental care is accessible to everyone.

Common questions

## Frequently asked questions

Does getting a filling hurt?

No, dental filling procedures at Krishna Multispeciality Dental Hospital are designed to be completely pain-free. We use advanced local anesthetics to numb the tooth and surrounding tissue, ensuring a comfortable experience at our Gudivada clinic.

How long do dental fillings last?

Composite (tooth-colored) fillings typically last 5 to 10 years, while premium ceramic restorations can last 10 to 20 years. The longevity of fillings at our Gudivada clinic depends on proper oral hygiene, material choice, and biting forces.

What's the difference between composite and amalgam fillings?

Composite fillings are tooth-colored, metal-free, and bond chemically to support the tooth structure, making them highly aesthetic. Amalgam fillings are silver-colored, durable, but contain trace metal and are visible. At Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada, we specialize in premium, natural-looking composite fillings.

What does a dental filling cost in Gudivada?

The cost of dental fillings in Gudivada depends on the size of the cavity, the type of tooth involved, and the selected material (composite, GIC, or ceramic). We offer competitive, transparent pricing at Krishna Dental. You can contact us through our website to obtain a personalized estimate.

What should I do after getting a filling?

After receiving a filling at our Gudivada clinic, avoid consuming extremely hot or cold beverages and hard/sticky foods until the anesthesia wears off. Continue brushing and flossing daily to protect the restoration margins.

When do I need to replace a filling?

Fillings require replacement if they crack, loosen, fall out, or if secondary decay develops beneath them. Dr. Vidya Sahithi recommends biannual check-ups at Krishna Multispeciality Dental Hospital in Gudivada to monitor the integrity of your fillings.

## Page: dental-implants-gudivada.html
**URL:** https://www.krishnadental.in/dental-implants-gudivada.html

Restorative Dentistry

# Dental Implants

Restore your smile with permanent, natural-looking teeth. Dental implants are the gold standard for replacing missing teeth — and they look, feel, and function like the real thing.

Book Consultation

Understanding implants

## What are dental implants?

A dental implant is a tiny titanium screw that replaces the root of a missing tooth. Over time, it fuses with your jawbone in a process called osseointegration. Once stable, an abutment (connector) is attached to the implant, and a natural-looking crown is fitted on top.

The result is a tooth that feels, looks, and functions just like your natural teeth. Unlike dentures, implants don't slip or shift. Unlike bridges, they don't damage adjacent teeth. And unlike tooth extraction, they preserve your jawbone and facial structure.

Is it right for you?

## Who benefits from implants

### Single missing tooth

Replace one tooth without affecting your neighbouring teeth. Your smile looks complete, and the implant functions like a natural tooth.

### Multiple missing teeth

Whether you're missing two teeth or several, we can place multiple implants or use implants to anchor a fixed bridge.

### Unstable dentures

If your denture slips or wobbles, implants can stabilise it. Just 2–4 implants can make a dramatic difference in comfort and confidence.

### Failed bridges or old restorations

If your old bridge or crown is failing, an implant can provide a long-lasting replacement without affecting other teeth.

Step by step

## The implant process

01

### Consultation & digital planning

We examine your mouth, take 3D scans, and assess your jawbone. Using advanced imaging, we plan the exact position, angle, and size of your implant for optimal results.

02

### Implant placement

Under local anaesthesia, we carefully place the titanium implant into your jawbone. The procedure is quick — usually 20–60 minutes — and you'll be awake and comfortable throughout.

03

### Healing & osseointegration

Over the next 3–6 months, the implant fuses with your bone, becoming a permanent part of your jaw. This creates an incredibly strong foundation for your new tooth.

04

### Abutment placement

Once healing is complete, we attach the abutment — a small connector — to the top of the implant. This takes just a few minutes and requires minimal discomfort.

05

### Crown fitting

We take impressions and create a custom crown that matches your natural teeth perfectly. Once fitted, your implant is ready to use — bite, chew, and smile with confidence.

Why choose us

## Implant expertise at Krishna Dental

### Experienced implant team

Our doctors have placed hundreds of successful implants with high long-term success rates. You're in skilled, trusted hands.

### Premium materials

We use the finest biocompatible titanium implants and high-quality crowns. No corners cut — your implant must last decades.

### Digital planning technology

3D imaging and surgical guides ensure precision placement. This means faster healing, better aesthetics, and fewer complications.

### Lifelong follow-up care

We don't just place your implant and disappear. We provide ongoing check-ups, cleanings, and support to keep your implant healthy for life.

Common questions

## Frequently asked questions

Is the implant procedure painful?

No, dental implant placement at Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada is a minor, comfortable surgical procedure. We perform the treatment under advanced local anesthesia to ensure you feel absolutely no pain — only slight pressure. Most patients find recovery is highly manageable with mild over-the-counter anti-inflammatories.

How long do dental implants last?

With excellent oral hygiene, dental implants placed at our Gudivada practice can last a lifetime. Titanium is biocompatible and naturally osseointegrates (fuses) with your jawbone. While the structural implant post remains permanently, the visible custom porcelain crown is designed to resist wear for decades.

What does a dental implant cost in Gudivada?

The cost of dental implants in Gudivada varies depending on bone density, number of missing teeth, and the implant system selected (such as Osstem or Straumann). Krishna Multispeciality Dental Hospital offers transparent treatment plans with easy EMI payment structures to fit your budget.

Am I a good candidate for dental implants?

Most adults in good systemic health with missing teeth are excellent candidates. During your consultation in Gudivada, Dr. Vidya uses 3D digital scans to check your jawbone density. If bone height is insufficient, we perform minor bone grafting first to establish a solid implant foundation.

How are implants different from dentures?

Dental implants are permanent, stable replacements anchored into the jawbone that preserve bone structure and restore 100% chewing force. Removable dentures rest on the gums, can slip while eating or speaking, and accelerate bone loss over time. Implants offer superior stability and comfort.

How long is the recovery time?

Most patients resume light daily activities within 24 to 48 hours. Complete gum healing takes 7 to 10 days. The titanium post then fuses with the bone over a 3 to 6 month osseointegration period before Dr. Vidya fits your final custom zirconia crown at our Gudivada clinic.

Book a consultation at Krishna Dental. Let's discuss your options and create a treatment plan that works for you.

## Page: dentures-gudivada.html
**URL:** https://www.krishnadental.in/dentures-gudivada.html

Prosthetic Dentistry

# Dentures

Comfortable, natural-looking tooth replacement. Restore your smile and confidence with custom-fitted dentures designed just for you.

Book Appointment

Know your options

## Understanding dentures

Dentures are custom-made replacements for missing teeth and surrounding tissues. They restore your ability to eat, speak, and smile with confidence — and you'll look as natural as ever.

Modern dentures are lighter, more comfortable, and more lifelike than ever before. At Krishna Dental, we craft each set with precision using premium materials, so they fit perfectly and feel like your own teeth.

Personalized solutions

## Types of dentures

### Complete Dentures

Replace all upper or lower teeth. Custom-crafted to match your jaw shape and face, they restore full function and appearance.

### Partial Dentures

Replace some missing teeth while preserving your natural ones. They attach to remaining teeth for stability and natural chewing.

### Flexible Dentures

Made with thermoplastic materials that are more flexible and comfortable. They're easier to insert and remove, and less likely to break.

### Implant-Supported

Anchored to dental implants for superior stability. They don't move or slip, and feel even more like natural teeth.

Your journey

## How we create your dentures

01

### Consultation

We discuss your needs, examine your mouth, and assess your bone structure. We help you choose the best type of dentures for your situation and budget.

02

### Impressions

We take detailed impressions and measurements of your mouth. These precise records are used to create dentures that fit perfectly and function naturally.

03

### Try-in

We show you a pre-final version to check fit, comfort, and appearance. Any adjustments are made at this stage to ensure they look and feel just right.

04

### Fitting & delivery

Your final dentures are inserted, and we make final adjustments. We show you how to insert, remove, and care for them properly.

05

### Adjustments & follow-up

We schedule follow-up visits to make fine adjustments and ensure your comfort. Your gums may change over time, and we'll help keep your dentures fitting perfectly.

Why choose us

## Why Krishna Dental

### Custom fit

Every set is custom-crafted to match your unique jaw structure and facial features for perfect comfort and appearance.

### Natural appearance

We match tooth color, shape, and gum contours to your facial features, so your dentures blend seamlessly with your smile.

### Comfortable materials

We use premium, biocompatible materials that are soft on your gums, durable, and designed for maximum comfort during daily wear.

### Ongoing support

We provide lifetime care and adjustments as your mouth changes. Our team is always here to ensure your dentures stay comfortable and functional.

Common questions

## Frequently asked questions

How long does it take to get used to dentures?

Most patients adapt to new dentures in Gudivada within 2 to 4 weeks. Dr. Vidya Sahithi Atluri guides patients through insertion, removal, and speech practice to make the transition at Krishna Multispeciality Dental Hospital as smooth as possible.

Can I eat normally with dentures?

Yes, but we advise starting with soft foods cut into small pieces while adjusting. Within a few weeks, patients at our Gudivada clinic can confidently return to enjoying their favorite foods, avoiding extremely sticky or hard items.

How long do dentures last?

With proper maintenance, custom dentures typically last 5 to 8 years. Over time, your jawbone structure naturally changes, meaning dentures at our Gudivada practice may require relining or replacement to maintain a snug, comfortable fit.

How do I clean and care for my dentures?

Brush your dentures daily with a soft-bristled brush and mild soap, then soak them in clean water or denture solution overnight. Always clean your gums and tongue, and visit Krishna Multispeciality Dental Hospital in Gudivada for regular checks.

What is the cost of dentures in Gudivada?

The cost of dentures in Gudivada varies depending on the type of restoration (complete, partial, or flexible) and materials used. Krishna Dental Hospital offers transparent, competitive pricing and flexible installment choices. Please visit our contact page to request a personalized quote.

Are dentures better than dental implants?

Both have distinct benefits. Dentures are highly cost-effective and suitable for replacing extensive tooth loss without surgery. Dental implants offer a permanent, bone-preserving solution that feels like natural teeth. Our Gudivada specialists will help you select the ideal option.

## Ready to restore your smile?

Schedule a consultation at Krishna Dental and discover your perfect denture solution. Walk-ins welcome.

## Common Dental Emergencies We Handle

### Severe Toothache Pain

Excruciating throbbing pain that wakes you up at night is often a sign of pulp infection. We offer immediate, pain-free emergency root canals to relieve distress.

### Knocked-Out or Loose Tooth

Accidental trauma? If a tooth has been knocked out, clean it gently, keep it moist in milk or saliva, and visit our clinic within 60 minutes to save the tooth.

### Broken, Cracked or Chipped Teeth

A broken tooth or lost crown exposes sensitive nerves, leading to intense pain and risks of infection. We provide same-day restorations, crowns, and bonding.

### Swollen Gums & Abscesses

A dental abscess is a serious bacterial infection that creates painful swellings. Immediate clinical drainage and antibiotic therapy are crucial to prevent systemic spread.

💡 Dental Emergency Guidelines (While On Your Way)

- For Severe Pain: Rinse with warm salt water. Avoid placing aspirin directly on the gums, as this causes tissue burns.
- For a Knocked-Out Tooth: Handle only by the chewing crown. Keep the tooth submerged in milk or a balanced salt solution.
- For Swelling: Apply a cold compress to the outside of your cheek for 10-minute intervals.

## Root Canal Treatment

Is a root canal treatment painful?

No, modern root canal treatments at Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada are designed to be completely pain-free. Led by our MDS specialists, we use advanced localized anesthetics and computer-guided rotary endodontics to ensure absolute comfort. The procedure is actually performed to immediately relieve the severe throbbing pain caused by a deep tooth infection, rather than causing pain.

How many appointments does a root canal take?

At our Gudivada clinic, a root canal typically takes 1 to 2 visits. For standard pulp infections, Dr. Vidya can perform a single-sitting root canal in under 60 minutes. However, if there is severe swelling, active abscesses, or complex canal anatomy, we schedule a second appointment to place clinical-grade sterile dressings inside the tooth to guarantee long-term treatment success before sealing it.

Do I absolutely need a dental crown (cap) after a root canal?

Yes, placing a custom dental crown (cap) is vital to preserve the tooth structure after a root canal. Because the procedure removes the infected blood and nerve supply, the tooth becomes dry and fragile over time. At Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada, we design custom Zirconia and CAD/CAM porcelain crowns that act as a protective shield, preventing fractures and restoring 100% chewing function.

What is the difference between a single-visit and multi-visit root canal?

A single-visit root canal at Krishna Dental in Gudivada is completed in one session and is recommended for uncomplicated tooth decay without active inflammation. If the tooth has severe swelling, a multi-visit root canal is performed; we clean the root canals and place a temporary sanitizing medicine inside the tooth for 7 to 10 days to eliminate bacteria before final obturation.

Can a root canal tooth get infected again?

Though rare, a root canal tooth can develop a secondary infection due to new decay, structural fractures, or a saliva leak. At Krishna Multispeciality Dental Hospital in Gudivada, we resolve these issues using advanced endodontic retreatment, which cleans and reseals the complex micro-canals to save your natural tooth.

How do I know if my tooth pulp is infected and needs a root canal?

Common symptoms indicating a deep pulp infection include persistent throbbing pain, sensitivity to hot and cold that lingers for minutes, discomfort when biting, swollen gums around the affected area, or a visible pimple-like bump on the gum line. If you notice these signs, our specialists in Gudivada recommend scheduling a digital X-ray evaluation immediately.

## Dental Implants

What is a dental implant and how does it work?

A dental implant is a permanent, medical-grade titanium post placed surgically into the jawbone to replace a missing tooth root. Through osseointegration, the implant fuses naturally with the bone over a few months. Dr. Vidya Sahithi (MDS) then secures a custom CAD/CAM porcelain or zirconia crown on top, providing a tooth replacement that looks, feels, and functions like a natural tooth.

Are dental implants safe and what is their success rate?

Yes, dental implants are extremely safe and are considered the gold standard for replacing missing teeth. When placed by experienced MDS implantologists using our clinic's highly sterile operatory protocols in Gudivada, dental implants have a clinical success rate of over 95% to 98%.

How long does the dental implant procedure take from start to finish?

At Krishna Dental Hospital, placing the titanium implant post is a minor, comfortable procedure taking under 45 minutes under local anesthesia. The entire process takes 3 to 6 months: we allow 3 to 4 months for the bone to fuse securely around the implant, followed by taking digital impressions to fabricate and place your final custom crown.

Do I need a bone graft before getting a dental implant?

A bone graft is only required if your jawbone lacks the thickness or volume to support an implant, which often happens after long-term tooth loss or severe gum disease. During your consultation at our Gudivada facility, we use a 3D CBCT scan to evaluate your bone density. If needed, a minor bone grafting procedure is performed to create a solid foundation for the implant.

How do I clean and care for my dental implant?

You care for dental implants just like natural teeth. We recommend brushing twice daily with a soft-bristled toothbrush, flossing daily (using implant-specific floss or a water flosser), and visiting Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada twice a year for routine professional cleanings to maintain healthy surrounding gums.

What is the difference between an implant and a dental bridge?

A dental implant is a standalone replacement that preserves neighboring teeth and stimulates the jawbone to prevent bone loss. A dental bridge requires grinding down and capping the healthy neighboring teeth to suspend a fake tooth in the middle. Implants are more durable, easier to clean, and offer a longer-term solution for patients in Gudivada.

## Orthodontics (Braces & Aligners)

What is the best age for children to start orthodontic evaluation?

The American Association of Orthodontists recommends children have their first orthodontic evaluation by age 7. At Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada, our specialists assess emerging permanent teeth and jaw growth early, allowing us to detect bite discrepancies and implement preventive or interceptive treatments when needed.

What is the difference between traditional metal braces and clear aligners?

Traditional braces use metal brackets and wires to guide teeth into position and cannot be removed by the patient. Clear aligners (such as Invisalign) are customized, transparent medical-grade plastic trays that are virtually invisible and removable for eating, brushing, and flossing. We offer both advanced systems at our Gudivada practice.

How long will I need to wear braces or clear aligners?

Active orthodontic treatment typically lasts between 12 to 24 months, depending on your individual bite complexity. During your initial orthodontic consultation at Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada, we use digital scans to map out your treatment timeline and show you how your teeth will move.

Does getting braces put on hurt?

Bonding orthodontic brackets to your teeth is a completely painless procedure. As your teeth begin to move during the first 3 to 5 days after placement or adjustments, you may feel mild soreness or pressure. At our Gudivada clinic, we provide detailed soft-food guides and comfort instructions to help minimize this temporary adjustment phase.

What foods must I avoid while wearing traditional braces?

To prevent damaging brackets or bending wires, patients wearing traditional braces should avoid hard, sticky, or highly crunchy foods. This includes popcorn, nuts, sticky candies, and chewing gum. Hard fruits like apples should be sliced into small pieces rather than bitten into directly.

Do I really need to wear a retainer after my orthodontic treatment?

Yes, wearing a retainer is essential to maintain your new smile. Teeth have a natural tendency to slowly shift back toward their original positions over time. At Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada, we provide custom retainers and long-term retention plans to keep your teeth permanently stabilized in their optimal alignment.

## Smile Makeover & Teeth Whitening

What is a digital smile makeover?

A digital smile makeover is a customized aesthetic plan designed to enhance your smile symmetry and facial harmony. Using digital dental design, Dr. Vidya combines cosmetic treatments such as thin porcelain veneers, dental crowns, teeth whitening, and gum contouring to transform your smile's shape, color, and alignment.

What is the difference between porcelain veneers and dental crowns?

A porcelain veneer is a thin ceramic shell bonded only to the visible front surface of a tooth, requiring minimal preparation, to correct aesthetic concerns like minor chips or gaps. A dental crown caps the entire tooth structure to restore strength, commonly used for teeth weakened by large cavities or root canals.

Is professional laser teeth whitening safe for my enamel?

Yes, professional teeth whitening at Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada is completely safe for your enamel. Under clinical supervision, we use neutral-pH whitening gels and specialized LED activation lights that lift deep stains without damaging your tooth structure or causing long-term sensitivity.

How long do the results of professional teeth whitening last?

Professional teeth whitening results generally last between 1 to 3 years. The longevity of your bright smile depends on dietary habits. To maintain results, we advise limiting highly pigmented beverages like tea and coffee, avoiding tobacco products, and maintaining regular preventive cleanings.

Can cosmetic veneers get stained like natural teeth?

No, high-quality porcelain veneers are highly resistant to staining. Porcelain is non-porous, meaning pigments from coffee, tea, or food do not penetrate the surface. However, to keep your gums healthy and maintain the bonding resin, regular checkups and cleanings at our Gudivada clinic are recommended.

What is composite bonding and how long does it last?

Composite bonding is a quick, minimally invasive cosmetic procedure where a tooth-colored composite resin is applied and shaped to repair minor chips, cracks, or spacing. Completed in a single visit at Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada, bonding results last 5 to 7 years with good home care and hygiene.

## General Dentistry & Oral Hygiene

How often should I get a professional dental cleaning and scaling?

We recommend getting a professional dental scaling and cleaning every 6 months to prevent plaque accumulation. For patients with a history of gum disease, deep periodontal pockets, or rapid tartar buildup, our team in Gudivada may recommend maintenance cleanings every 3 to 4 months.

Does scaling (dental cleaning) make my teeth loose or sensitive?

No, professional scaling does not loosen teeth. Scaling uses gentle ultrasonic vibrations and water flow to remove calculus (tartar) that regular brushing cannot clean. Removing this buildup might cause temporary temperature sensitivity for a few days, but it is essential to prevent chronic bone loss and gum disease.

Why do my gums bleed when I brush or floss?

Gums bleed due to plaque buildup along the gumline, which causes inflammation (gingivitis). With regular flossing, soft brushing, and a professional scaling appointment at Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada, gingivitis can be completely reversed. If bleeding continues, it is important to schedule an evaluation.

What is the difference between dental plaque and tartar (calculus)?

Plaque is a soft, sticky film of bacteria that constantly forms on your teeth and can be brushed away daily. If not removed within 24 to 48 hours, plaque hardens into tartar (calculus). Tartar cannot be removed by brushing and requires professional scaling tools at our Gudivada clinic.

At what age should I take my child to their first dentist appointment?

We recommend scheduling your child's first dental visit when their first tooth appears, or by their first birthday. Early visits at Krishna Dental Hospital in Gudivada focus on monitoring jaw development, guiding parents on infant oral care, and building a positive, comfortable relationship with the dentist.

What are pit and fissure sealants and how do they prevent pediatric cavities?

Pit and fissure sealants are thin, protective coatings applied to the deep chewing grooves of a child's permanent molars. The sealant bonds to the tooth, acting as a physical barrier that prevents food particles and cavity-causing bacteria from getting trapped in hard-to-clean grooves.

How can I treat chronic bad breath (halitosis) permanently?

Treating bad breath starts with diagnosing its cause, which is often bacterial plaque, untreated cavities, gum inflammation, or dry mouth. A professional scaling and dental exam at our Gudivada clinic, combined with targeted hygiene routines, can effectively eliminate oral bacteria and restore fresh breath.

Understanding the treatment

## What is orthodontic treatment?

Orthodontic treatment straightens teeth and corrects bite problems using braces or clear aligners. This improves not just your appearance, but also your oral health and jaw function.

Straighter teeth are easier to clean, less prone to decay and gum disease, and can improve your overall quality of life. At Krishna Dental, we offer multiple options — from traditional metal braces to invisible clear aligners — so you can choose what works best for your lifestyle and goals.

Braces options

## Types of braces

### Metal Braces

The most reliable and effective option. Durable stainless steel brackets and wires work quickly and are highly customizable for all correction types.

### Ceramic Braces

Tooth-coloured brackets blend in beautifully with your smile. Nearly invisible while still being as effective as metal braces for most cases.

### Self-Ligating Braces

Advanced brackets eliminate the need for elastic bands. Result: faster tooth movement, fewer adjustments, and more comfort during treatment.

### Clear Aligners

Virtually invisible, removable trays gradually straighten your teeth. Perfect for those wanting a discreet solution without visible brackets.

04

05

### Retainer phase
